facts.statement: The genus Bullerichthys was described by Dennis and Miles in 1980.
Bullerichthys lived during the Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.
Bullerichthys is an extinct genus containing only one species of arthrodire placoderm from the Early Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Bullerichthys is an extinct monospecific genus of arthrodire placoderm from the Early Frasnian stage of the Late Devonian period.

facts.statement: Fossils of Bullerichthys have been found in the Gogo Formation in the Kimberley region of Australia.
facts.quote: Fossils are found in the Gogo Formation of the Kimberley region of Australia.

facts.statement: Researchers believed Bullerichthys was durophagous, feeding on hard-shelled creatures like mollusks.
facts.quote: It was thought to be durophagous, meaning that it preyed upon hard-shelled creatures such as mollusks.

facts.statement: Bullerichthys is a basal member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which is part of the major clade Pachyosteomorphi within Eubrachythoraci.
facts.quote: Bullerichthys is a basal member of the clade Aspinothoracidi, which belongs to the clade Pachyosteomorphi, one of the two major clades within Eubrachythoraci.

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Bullerichthys is Aspinothoracidi.
Bullerichthys is classified in the class Placodermi.
Bullerichthys lived between 382.31 and 379 million years ago during the Frasnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Frasnian to Frasnian (382.31 to 379 million years ago)
